title: Prepositions of Place
definition: Prepositions of place explain where someone or something is, where it is going, or where it comes from. Some German place prepositions take a fixed case; two-way prepositions can take dative for location and accusative for destination or direction.

rules.title: Where? — location with dative
rules.explanation: For location with two-way prepositions, ask wo? and usually use the dative.

examples.german: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
examples.english: The book is lying on the table.

examples.german: Die Lampe hängt über dem Tisch.
examples.english: The lamp is hanging above the table.

rules.title: Where to? — direction with accusative
rules.explanation: With two-way prepositions, ask wohin? and use the accusative when something moves to a destination.

examples.german: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.
examples.english: I put the book onto the table.
I am going into the kitchen.

examples.german: Er hängt das Bild über das Sofa.
examples.english: He hangs the picture above the sofa.

rules.title: Common two-way prepositions
rules.explanation: The main two-way prepositions are an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, and zwischen.

examples.german: Der Stuhl steht neben dem Tisch.
examples.english: The chair is next to the table.

examples.german: Der Hund liegt unter dem Bett.
examples.english: The dog is lying under the bed.

examples.german: Ich stelle den Stuhl neben den Tisch.
examples.english: I put the chair next to the table.

rules.title: Fixed prepositions of place
rules.explanation: Some common place prepositions take a fixed case: aus, bei, nach, von, zu take dative; durch takes accusative.

examples.english: I am at my friend's place.
I am going to the train station.

rules.title: Useful contractions
rules.explanation: Common contractions include im = in dem, ins = in das, am = an dem, ans = an das, zum = zu dem, and zur = zu der.

examples.english: I am going to the cinema.
We meet at the train station.

two_way_rule.wo: Dative for location: Das Glas steht auf dem Tisch.
two_way_rule.wohin: Accusative for destination: Ich stelle das Glas auf den Tisch.

common_mistakes.wrong: Das Buch liegt auf den Tisch.
common_mistakes.correct: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
common_mistakes.explanation: This describes a location (wo?), so use dative.
This describes movement into a destination (wohin?), so use accusative.

memorization_list.english: where? — location, often dative with two-way prepositions
where to? — destination, often accusative with two-way prepositions

mastery_goal: You can describe locations and destinations and choose dative versus accusative with common two-way prepositions.
